patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the icon should open and close a hidden navigation panel or drawer for mobile. Because this is a disclosure-style nav, it also implies state changes such as expanded/collapsed and likely an overlay or slide-in panel.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether the menu opens as a full-screen overlay, side drawer, or dropdown panel, nor whether nested nav items exist inside it.

patterns_found.behavior_notes: The search field requires submit behavior at minimum; desktop explicitly suggests a search action button. Focus handling, keyboard submission, and possibly query-state updates are implied.

patterns_found.behavior_notes: At minimum, JavaScript may validate non-empty input before submission and manage focus/error feedback if submission is blocked. This is especially likely for the lower standalone input area that resembles a signup/contact field.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Interactive controls in the sketches include the mobile hamburger menu and multiple form inputs/buttons; the mobile menu especially implies programmatic focus movement when opened and closed.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When the mobile menu opens, focus should move into the revealed navigation and return to the trigger on close. Inputs and any revealed interactive regions should participate in a logical keyboard flow.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No modal or explicit overlay is drawn, so the extent of focus trapping versus simple focus placement depends on the eventual menu implementation.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply relatively light JavaScript overall: the main cross-viewport behavior is form handling for visible inputs, while the primary mobile-specific interaction is a hamburger-triggered navigation reveal. No tabs, accordions, modals, infinite loading, sticky navigation, or explicit dropdowns are visually indicated. Desktop appears mostly static aside from search/input submission, whereas mobile adds the only clearly structural JS interaction through the collapsed navigation control.
